The report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) examines grant programs awarded by the Departments of Health and Human Services (HHS), Labor (DOL), and Justice (DOJ) from 2007 to 2015, focusing on those subject to statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring for which nonprofits were eligible to be primary recipients.

HHS identified one grant program, the PATH program, which was subject to such restrictions but no grants were awarded to nonprofit organizations. DOL identified 18 programs, 931 grantees, and 19 potential faith-based organizations (FBOs). DOJ identified at least 34 relevant grant programs, 604 grantees, and 25 potential FBOs.

Of the 117 potential FBOs identified across the three agencies, nine faith-based grantees, all of which were awarded DOJ grants, certified that they were exempt from statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring. These grantees stated that hiring individuals of the same faith was crucial to their mission and organizational success.

DOJ, DOL, and HHS all provide information on statutory restrictions on religious-based hiring and exemption processes to grant applicants and recipients through various methods. However, some potential FBOs that did not certify for an exemption could not recall seeing the information in the grant application or award documentation.

The total funding awarded to the nine exempted grantees was approximately $3.2 million, which is less than 1% of the $804 million in grants that DOJ awarded during this period that are subject to statutory restrictions.

The report concludes that while the agencies require grantees seeking exemptions to self-certify, they vary in how they review and approve requests. DOJ does not review self-certifications, while DOL requires grantees to submit their request for review and approval by the Assistant Secretary. HHS has only one grant program subject to a statutory restriction on religious-based hiring and for which FBOs are eligible to be primary recipients, but no faith-based recipients were identified during the study period.
